method: Web sweep for explicit mentions of the AC BO Hackathon outside the hackathon's own website and GitHub org: LinkedIn, personal CVs and sites, paper acknowledgments and citations, news, blogs, social media, and follow-on repos. Only verified hits with URLs. LinkedIn is only partially indexable without login, so this undercounts. Additional per-person mentions are recorded in trajectories.json (hackathon_mention field).

hits.quote_or_summary: Lists the hackathon as a CV/experience entry: 'Team lead in Bayesian Optimization Hackathon for Chemistry and Materials... use BO with local GP to find Covalent Organic Frameworks (COF) with the best methane storage capacity.'

hits.person_or_org: Gary Tom, Stanley Lo, Samantha Corapi, Alan Aspuru-Guzik, Benjamin Sanchez-Lengeling (arXiv paper)
hits.quote_or_summary: Peer-reviewed paper 'Ranking over Regression for Bayesian Optimization and Molecule Selection' (APL Machine Learning 2025) acknowledges: 'This project was also part of the Acceleration Consortium Bayesian optimization hackathon.' Grew out of the RBBO hackathon project P44.

hits.person_or_org: Molecular Quantum Solutions / Bio Innovation Institute (Quantum Innovation Challenge)
hits.quote_or_summary: A later challenge's acknowledgements credit the event: 'We thank Sterling G. Baird and the rest of the organizing team for the Bayesian Optimization Hackathon for Chemistry and Materials.' MQS ran hackathon project 42.
A follow-on microscopy ML hackathon credits it as a template in its README: 'Built up on [LLM in Chemistry and Materials hackathon] and [BO hackathon](https://ac-bo-hackathon.github.io/)'.
RAMBO-I project repo: 'Check out our poster for the AC-BO-Hackathon.'
ACBO-Feat repo: 'This is a repo created for the 2024 AC BO Hackathon' (Project 8), with poster and video presentation; project continued after the event and fed 2025 papers.

best_batchers repo: 'Bayesian Optimization Hackathon for Chemistry and Materials, Project 15: Adaptive Batch Sizes for Bayesian Optimization of Reaction Yield.' Team later published Cost-informed Bayesian reaction optimization (Digital Discovery 2024).
BlenDS repo: 'Started as a project for the AC Bayesian Optimization Hackathon in March 2024.' Includes hackathon poster.
BOMS-ProBs repo: 'This is a repository for the BO Hackathon hosted by Acceleration Consortium for Chemistry and Materials' (Project 34), with hackathon poster.

SeroOpt repo README references 'AC BO = Acceleration Consortium Bayesian Optimization hackathon entries' and links hackathon project pages 30 and 31; SeroOpt became the software behind a Digital Discovery 2025 paper.
bayes-warmup repo, described as 'AC BO Hackathon Team bayes-warmup' (Project 27).
ac-bo-hackathon repo: 'Efficient Protein Mutagenesis using Bayesian Optimization', with Ben Weiser, Sylvester Zhang, Jerome Genzling.
AC-BO-HACKATHON-2024 repo and personal GitHub page: 'Project 17: Comparative Analysis of Acquisition Functions in Bayesian Optimization for Drug Discovery'.
Hackathon_Ac_BO repo: 'This program has been made for the Bayesian Optimization Hackathon for Chemistry and Materials'.
Shared his hackathon project SimpleGPT-BO (Project 4) on LinkedIn: 'Join us in democratizing Bayesian Optimization with SimpleGPT-BO.'

Participant reflection on the Accelerated Discovery community forum: thanked the organizers, especially enjoyed 'the GatherTown posters where we could interact with people around the world'; planned to submit the RBBO project to NeurIPS 2024 (it was published in APL Machine Learning 2025).
Third-party 'awesome' resource list includes the hackathon under AI resources, linking ac-bo-hackathon.github.io/projects/.

Organizer's public LinkedIn post announcing the preprint, calling it 'one of the most rewarding events' he has hosted, noting 44 teams and 120 active participants. (Organizer, not participant; included for completeness.)

verified_negatives: Andy Anker's ScattBO GitHub repo and the DTU/MAX IV news coverage of his self-driving lab do not mention the hackathon.
The Honegumi arXiv paper (Baird, Falkowski, Sparks) does not mention the hackathon.
The Matterhorn Studio hackathons page confirms it sponsored the prize but is the sponsor's own channel.
